thread:
maria: Heads-up: CI perf alert after the merge to main (PR #8428). p99 jumped on the short-seq tests and we're seeing a compile storm in the canary region. :frowning:
ryan: Ugh. Which merge? any quick diffs? :eyes:
sophia: Looks like the autotune heuristic change from last week is implicated — it started preferring the 'small-batch-packed' kernel for <32 tokens. That kernel compiles ~3x slower and triggers cold compile saturation if cache misses spike.
maria: Exact numbers from the perf job: before merge p99 ~48ms, after merge p99 ~118ms on the short-seq microbench. compile queue length spiked from ~2 -> ~37. KV cache evictions per-min jumped 7x. Logs attached in the job.
ci-bot: [CI] perf/regression short-seq p99 = +70ms (baseline 48ms -> current 118ms). Job: https://ci.internal/jobs/5123
anjali: Can we bisect to the commit that rolled the heuristic? I can run the kernel-autopick bisect script if you want.
ryan: Yes please. Start with range: origin/main~10..origin/main. Also add a quick check to pin the heuristic to previous weights so we can stop the canary oscillation.
sophia: I'm running a narrowed bisect now: ./scripts/bisect_kernel_autopick.sh --commits=origin/main~6..origin/main --test=short-seq-quick --repeat=3
ryan: If the bisect isolates it to the heuristic change, we should either revert the heuristic PR (if it's the root) or add an override: if seq_len < 48 && batch_size <= 8 prefer 'small-batch-legacy' kernel. That buys us time.
maria: Revert candidate is commit abcdef12 from PR #8360. Sophia, any ETA on bisect?
sophia: First pass done, failing commit is abcdef12 (the autotune model weight update). Confirming with a quick repro on my workstation now.
sophia: Repro steps:
```
# run short-seq repro
python -m bench.shortseq --model gpt-small --seq-len 16 --iters 200
# before: kernel=small-batch-legacy compile_time median 22ms
# after: kernel=small-batch-packed compile_time median 71ms
```
ryan: Ok, plan: 1) pin heuristic override in canary config, 2) revert abcdef12 on main if necessary, 3) add stricter compile concurrency limit to avoid queue flood. Who owns the canary deploy config?
anjali: I can push a canary override. Patch: add to config/profiles/canary.yaml:
```
kernel_override:
  short_seq_preference: small-batch-legacy
```
I'll roll to canary immediately.
maria: Please also mute perf alerts for that canary run until we validate to avoid noise.
build-bot: Deploy queued: canary override patch pushed by anjali. Rollout to canary region starts in 30s. Change-id: canary-override-20260318-1
ci-bot: Triggered: perf/regression short-seq quick job to validate override — job 5124.
sophia: Local repro with pinned override: p99 back to ~52ms, compile queue stable at ~3. Looks good.
ryan: Good. We'll hold on reverting main for now. Still need a follow-up: update autotune training to penalize kernels with long cold compile time, and add a KB entry documenting tradeoffs.
maria: Agreed. Action items:
- anjali: monitor canary perf job 5124, leave revert on standby (ETA 30m)
- sophia: open PR to add compile-time penalty in autotune loss (and add unit test)
- ryan: add compile concurrency guard to runtime to hard cap compile queue growth
- maria: write a postmortem if revert is required

maria: Thanks all. Adding :eyes: on job results. If canary stays stable I'll mark this as rollout-blocked -> mitigated.
ryan: thx — ping me if job 5124 still shows >+20ms
anjali: job 5124 green. p99 55ms. Rolling the override to other small regions.
sophia: Filed follow-up: https://git.internal/rw/inference/issues/1294 — autotune compile-penalty
maria: closing loop: no revert required. leaving a note in the release thread and tracking follow-ups. :white_check_mark:
